full_judgment: 7. Mr. Majid has no explanation as to why the prayer could not be made earlier at proper stage of the suit after framing of the issues. We have referred to the submission made by Mr Habib on the facts involved upon which the other side sought for a decision. In this revision we are not called upon to decide whether on the materials on record the suit was actually hit by bar of res judicata; we will see whether the learned Judge has exercised his discretion in arbitrary and unreasonable manner in rejecting the defendants' prayer for determination of the issue first. We have already observed that the petitioners have no explanation as to why at the proper preliminary stage the prayer could not be made. Making the prayer on the date fixed for final hearing is to frustrate the object of Order 14 rule 2 and Order 15 rule 3 to avoid protracted litigation and unnecessary expenditure. On this ground alone the learned Judge must be held to have properly exercised his discretion in rejecting the belated prayer and thus avoiding a pieacemeal disposal of the suit. In this connection the decision cited by Mr. Habib may be referred to, wherein it has been held that where the parties to a suit are at issue on several questions all such questions should be heard together and disposed of by one judgment so that in case of the reversal of the trial Court's decision on certain issues, there may not be any necessity for remand of the suit for disposal of the undisposed of issues.
